meta.description: Central repository of plain-language questions about Indian public data, mapped to a live breakdown. Central-government questions resolve to live data now; municipal questions are seeded and will be back-filled as we ingest public municipal portals.

questions.q: What is the current RBI repo rate?
questions.answer: The RBI's policy repo rate is 5.25% (as at 2 Sep 2026). It's the rate at which the RBI lends to banks and sets the direction for your loan EMIs.

questions.q: Why are my loan EMIs going up or down?
questions.answer: Bank lending rates track the RBI repo rate. When the repo rate rises, floating-rate EMIs usually rise too; when it falls, they ease.
CRR (3%) is the share of deposits banks must park as cash with the RBI; SLR (18%) is the share they must hold in safe assets like government bonds.

questions.q: How much are India's forex reserves right now?
questions.answer: India's foreign exchange reserves are about ₹69.8 lakh crore (week ended 21 Aug 2026), most of it in foreign currency assets, plus gold, SDRs and the IMF position.

questions.q: How much gold does the RBI hold in reserves?
questions.answer: Gold makes up roughly ₹10.9 lakh crore of India's reserves — about 16% of the total.

questions.q: Why do foreign exchange reserves matter?
questions.answer: Reserves cushion the rupee against shocks and cover imports. A rising reserve pile generally signals a stronger external position.

questions.q: How much will the government spend this year?
questions.answer: The Union Budget 2025-26 plans total expenditure of about ₹50.7 lakh crore.

questions.q: Where does my tax rupee actually go?
questions.answer: Of every rupee the government spends, 22 paise goes to states' share of taxes, 20 paise to interest on past debt, and the rest to schemes, defence, subsidies and pensions.

questions.q: How much of the budget just pays off old debt?
questions.answer: Interest payments take 20 paise of every rupee the central government spends — the second-largest single item.

questions.q: How much does India budget for defence?
questions.answer: Defence accounts for about 8 paise of every rupee of central spending in 2025-26.

questions.q: What is the fiscal deficit target?
questions.answer: The fiscal deficit for 2025-26 is targeted at 4.4% of GDP — the gap between what the government spends and earns.

questions.q: What is the rupee-dollar rate today?
questions.answer: The FBIL reference rate is about ₹94.97 per US dollar (2 Sep 2026).

questions.q: How is my municipal property tax calculated?
questions.answer: Property tax is set by your urban local body, usually from built-up area, usage and a locality rate. We're building live municipal breakdowns — this question is seeded pending portal ingestion.

questions.q: Where do my municipal water charges go?
questions.answer: Water charges fund your city's supply, treatment and pipelines. Live ward-level data ingestion is on the roadmap.

questions.q: How much does my ward get in the city budget?
questions.answer: City corporations publish ward-wise allocations, but rarely in a readable form. We're building this — the question is seeded in the central repository.

questions.q: Who is responsible for garbage collection in my area?
questions.answer: Solid-waste management is a municipal function funded from the city budget and user charges. Live municipal data is pending ingestion.
